s1.syndrome_frame: febrile illness with severe sore throat, neck pain, and neurological symptoms
salient_findings: Pharyngeal erythema with enlarged tonsils and whitish tonsillar exudates
Altered consciousness and generalized tonic-clonic seizures
CSF analysis showing leukocyte count of 250 cells/mm3
Diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement on CT head/neck
key_facts: Enlarged tonsils with whitish tonsillar exudates
No lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly on palpation
Altered consciousness and generalized tonic-clonic seizures
Post-ictal drowsiness and unresponsiveness to verbal commands

shortlist.label: Epstein-Barr virus encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive EBV DNA in CSF and clinical presentation of fever, sore throat, and neurological symptoms

shortlist.label: Infectious mononucleosis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive viral capsid antigen (VCA) IgM and clinical presentation of fever, sore throat, and lymphadenopathy

shortlist.label: Herpes simplex virus encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Severe neurological symptoms, including altered consciousness and seizures, which are consistent with HSV encephalitis

shortlist.label: Enteroviral meningitis
shortlist.why_kept: CSF analysis showing leukocyte count of 250 cells/mm3 and clinical presentation of fever, sore throat, and neck pain

shortlist.label: Cytomegalovirus encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of fever, sore throat, and neurological symptoms, although less likely than EBV encephalitis given the positive EBV DNA in CSF

raw.rationale: The presence of positive viral capsid antigen (VCA) IgM, absent Epstein-Barr nuclear antigen (EBNA), and positive EBV DNA in CSF strongly supports this diagnosis, along with the clinical presentation of fever, sore throat, and neurological symptoms.

rejected.label: Infectious mononucleosis
rejected.why: While the patient has some symptoms consistent with infectious mononucleosis, such as fever and sore throat, the presence of neurological symptoms and positive EBV DNA in CSF points more specifically to encephalitis.

rejected.label: Herpes simplex virus encephalitis
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence provided for HSV infection, such as positive HSV PCR in CSF, and the serology points towards EBV infection.

rejected.label: Enteroviral meningitis
rejected.why: The CSF analysis and clinical presentation do not specifically suggest enteroviral infection, and the presence of EBV DNA in CSF supports EBV encephalitis over enteroviral meningitis.

rejected.label: Cytomegalovirus encephalitis
rejected.why: There is no evidence provided for CMV infection, and the serology and CSF findings support EBV encephalitis as the diagnosis.
